title: Oral Bacillus subtilis attenuates house dust mite-induced atopic dermatitis and is associated with altered mucosal immune responses.
abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease often presenting in infancy and increases the risk of developing other atopic disorders including food allergy, allergic rhinitis, and asthma. The rising prevalence of allergic diseases correlates with increasingly sterile living environments and reduced exposure to bacteria. This study hypothesized that exposure to nonpathogenic bacteria could help educate the immune system toward tolerance to innocuous allergens. Oral delivery of th...

title: Effects of a 12-week multi-strain probiotics supplementation on circulating endotoxin and antioxidant enzymes among overweight/obese Saudi adults: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
abstract: Several clinical trials have indicated the favorable effects of probiotics in lowering the risk of chronic diseases such as obesity; however, few of them have explored the potential in altering obesity-related biomarkers, and the present study aimed to fill this gap.

title: Unlocking the potential of microalga (Arthrospira platensis) as a sustainable feed supplement for sheep: impacts on rumen dynamics, productive performance, health and product quality.
abstract: Sheep production plays a crucial role in the global meat market, with nutrition being a primary factor influencing ruminant productivity and well-being. Growing consumer demand for healthy animal products has driven a shift towards natural feed supplements, spurring significant interest in nutrient-dense microalgae like Arthrospira platensis (AP), often referred to as the "feed supplement of the future". Arthrospira platensis thrives in warm, alkaline waters (pH 8.5-11.0) and is renowned for its...

title: Probiotics Boost Fecal Short-Chain Fatty Acids and Reshape Gut Microbial Communities in an MPTP-Induced Parkinson's Disease Mouse Model.
abstract: Gut dysbiosis has been evidenced to play an important role in the pathology of Parkinson's disease (PD). Abnormalities in short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) act as key pathological drivers of PD pathogenesis. This study aimed to investigate the efficacy of a probiotic mixture against gut dysbiosis in PD, and to elucidate its regulatory mechanism targeting the microbiota-SCFAs axis. A 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP)-induced PD mouse model was established, and a probiotic mixture ...

title: Gut microbiome-based interventions to prevent ICU-acquired infections: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Gut microbiome colonization with potential pathogens is common and often precedes clinical infection in the intensive care unit (ICU). Two key gut microbiome-based interventions seek to prevent infections yet use opposite approaches: selective digestive decontamination (SDD) utilizes antibiotics to eliminate potential pathogens, whereas biotic supplementation (prebiotics, probiotics, or synbiotics) aims to enrich beneficial microbes. In the absence of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) directly...

title: Effects of dietary nitrate supplementation in team sport athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Dietary nitrate (NO3 -), typically provided as beetroot juice, increases nitric oxide availability and may reduce the oxygen cost of exercise, improve muscle oxygenation, and delay fatigue. Evidence in team sport athletes, however, remains limited and has not been comprehensively synthesized. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluate the effects of NO3 - supplementation on team sport-specific performance and related physiological and biochemical outcomes.
journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

title: Study protocol: efficacy and safety of Limosilactobacillus fermentum WIS32 as an adjunctive treatment for major depressive disorder-a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is one of the leading causes of disability worldwide. Although antidepressant medications are widely used as first-line treatments, a substantial proportion of patients experience insufficient therapeutic response or limited tolerability, highlighting the need for additional safe and effective adjunctive treatment strategies. In recent years, growing evidence has suggested that the microbiota-gut-brain axis may play an important modulatory role in the onset, maint...

title: Effects of dietary acorn supplementation on growth performance, nutrient digestibility and gut microbial metabolism in finishing pigs.
abstract: The sustainable utilization of alternative feed resources is increasingly important for improving nutrient efficiency and promoting intestinal health in pig production. Acorns are abundant plant-derived resources containing carbohydrates, dietary fiber, and bioactive compounds; however, their potential as a functional feed ingredient for finishing pigs remains insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to investigate the effects of dietary acorn supplementation on growth performance, nutrien...

title: Association between preoperative omega-3/vitamin E supplementation and tissue inflammatory and redox biomarkers in persistent apical periodontitis.
abstract: To evaluate whether preoperative supplementation with an omega-3/vitamin E-containing formulation was associated with differences in the tissue inflammatory and redox biomarker profile of persistent asymptomatic periapical lesions requiring endodontic microsurgery.

title: Biofilm-State Probiotics for Seafood Safety: Multifactorial Mechanisms and Emerging Biocontrol Strategies.
abstract: Biofilms formed by foodborne pathogens on seafood and processing surfaces can withstand refrigeration, cleaning, and chemical sanitization, allowing them to persist as reservoirs for recurrent product contamination. The antimicrobial and antibiofilm activities of probiotic bacteria, particularly lactic acid bacteria (LAB), are well documented, but the physiological state in which a probiotic is applied has received far less attention. Biofilm-state probiotics (BSPs), defined here as probiotic mi...
journal: Comprehensive reviews in food science and food safety

title: Train hard, recover smart: the supplement framework to enhance exercise recovery in recreational and elite-level athletes.
abstract: Background: Exercise-induced inflammation and muscle damage are frequent consequences of structured physical activity that facilitate muscle growth and subsequent training adaptations. Performance improvements are strongly dependent upon athletes' capacity to successfully recover from previous sessions or challenging efforts, particularly when opportunities to rest and recover are limited. Nutritional practices centered around acute or chronic ingestion of certain foods or dietary bioactive comp...
journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

title: Sustainable poultry growth through indigenous probiotic feed development.
abstract: Indigenous probiotics adapted to local production conditions may provide an alternative to imported feed additives. In this study, Bacillus subtilis was isolated and characterized and a laboratory-produced preparation in broilers was evaluated. Fifty presumptive isolates were obtained from 50 samples of buffalo feces, poultry gut, and buffalo gut and screened sequentially: 30 were gram-positive rods, 20 were catalase- and oxidase-positive and spore-forming, all were non-haemolytic and lipolytic,...

title: Selenoprotein Network Dysfunction in Neurodegenerative Diseases-Dissecting Brain Distribution, Neuroprotection, and Selenium Supplementation Challenges.
abstract: Selenium is an essential trace element in humans and, together with 25 selenoproteins, plays a critical role in maintaining central nervous system homeostasis. Alterations in the selenoprotein network are increasingly implicated in multiple neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease. Although the brain possesses a selenium-prioritization mechanism that preserves selenium under conditions of systemic deficiency, the biological effects of selenium exhibit a U...

title: Self-reported health-related quality of life among regular multivitamin-mineral supplement users: a weighted pooled observational analysis of 2,600 adults from four Asia Pacific countries.
abstract: Multivitamin-mineral (MVM) supplements are widely used across the Asia Pacific; however, real-world, validated patient-reported evidence on immune function, mental well-being and energy remains limited. The aim of the study is to evaluate the relationship between daily MVM consumption and quality of life using validated patient-reported outcomes (PROs) measures across pooled adult cohorts in the Asia-Pacific region and assess perceived immune and energy support among daily versus non-daily MVM u...
journal: Journal of health, population, and nutrition

title: Probiotic potential of Blautia producta L1 in mitigating Eimeria tenella-induced intestinal inflammation and dysbiosis in chickens.
abstract: The capacity of Blautia to restore microbial homeostasis and attenuate intestinal inflammation highlights its potential as a promising microbial therapeutic for poultry coccidiosis.

title: Alginate-whey protein/chitosan microencapsulation of Lactobacillus casei ZGP-Lca.25 enhances viability and modulates apoptosis in colorectal cancer cells.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and resistance to conventional therapies highlights the need for novel adjunctive treatment strategies. Although Lactobacillus casei (L. casei) has shown promising anticancer potential, its poor survival under gastrointestinal conditions limits its therapeutic application. In this study, we investigated whether alginate-whey protein microencapsulation with a chitosan coating could overcome the poor g...

title: Effect of probiotic, prebiotic, and synbiotic supplementation on anemia in hemodialysis patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: Anemia is common in hemodialysis patients and reduces quality of life. Gut dysbiosis may contribute. Biotic supplements (probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics) could help, but evidence is uncertain. This review evaluated their effects on hemoglobin, hematocrit, ferritin, and TIBC.

title: Bioactive composition and in vitro bioactivity of postbiotics from mixed probiotic cultures: antimicrobial, antioxidant, and antidiabetic effects.
abstract: Postbiotics, bioactive metabolites produced during probiotic fermentation, are increasingly recognized for their health-promoting properties and potential applications in functional foods and natural biopreservation. This study evaluated the bioactive composition and in vitro bioactivities of postbiotics derived from defined mixed cultures of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG (ATCC 53103), Lactiplantibacillus plantarum (DSM 9843), Bifidobacterium longum (35624), and Bifidobacterium breve (DSM 1660...

title: Genomic characterization of Pediococcus acidilactici AB01 isolated from Algerian Targui camel milk: insights into safety, probiotic-associated traits, and functional potential.
abstract: Pediococcus acidilactici displays substantial strain-level variation, requiring genome-resolved evaluation of new food-associated isolates. This study characterized P. acidilactici AB01, isolated from raw milk of Algerian Targui camels, and used previously generated in vitro observations only to contextualize genomic predictions. Illumina sequencing yielded a 2,117,438-bp draft genome with 42.0% GC content, 36 contigs, and an N50 of 389,234 bp. BUSCO recovered 99.2% complete markers, whereas Che...

title: A bioactive gelatin/tannic acid/Ginkgo biloba leaf polysaccharide dual-network microgel enhances oral delivery of Bacillus amyloliquefaciens LJ1 and alleviates patulin-induced gut-liver axis injury.
abstract: Patulin (PAT) is a common mycotoxin that disrupts the gut-liver axis and is difficult to remove from foods. Herein, a bioactive dual-network gelatin/tannic acid/Ginkgo biloba leaf polysaccharide (GTG) microgel was developed for oral delivery of Bacillus amyloliquefaciens LJ1. Compared with gelatin/tannic acid microgels, GTG showed a more compact structure, higher encapsulation efficiency, improved probiotic viability, stronger mucoadhesion, enhanced gastric protection, and sustained intestinal r...

title: Lactoferrin-phosphatidylcholine composite emulsions enhance gastrointestinal, thermal, and storage stability of Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG.
abstract: Probiotics exert multiple beneficial effects on host, but their activity may decline during transportation, storage, and gastrointestinal digestion. Inspired by the natural structure of the milk fat globule membrane (MFGM), this study developed an oil-in-water (O/W) emulsion using lactoferrin (LF) and phosphatidylcholine (PC) to encapsulate Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) and investigated its effects on LGG stability. Infrared and fluorescence spectroscopy, together with zeta-potential measurem...

title: AI-assisted precision microbial control in probiotic fruit-vegetable beverages: a critical review.
abstract: Probiotic fruit-vegetable beverages present a safety-functionality challenge because pathogenic and spoilage microorganisms must be controlled while viable, functionally relevant probiotic strains, sensory quality, and bioactive attributes are retained. Thermal and non-thermal preservation technologies can reduce microbial risk but are not intrinsically selective, and their effects remain strain-, matrix-, process-, and equipment-dependent. This critical review evaluates the evidence supporting ...

title: Preclinical safety evaluation of Vernolac, a commercially available polyherbal nutraceutical comprising Vernonia zeylanica, Nigella sativa, Hemidesmus indicus, Smilax glabra, and Leucas zeylanica, in Wistar rats.
abstract: Vernolac is a commercially available polyherbal formulation comprising Vernonia zeylanica aerial parts, Nigella sativa seeds, Hemidesmus indicus roots, Smilax glabra rhizome, and Leucas zeylanica aerial parts. Although previous in vitro studies have demonstrated the anticancer potential of Vernolac and its active ingredients, safety data are available only for some of the plant ingredients of Vernolac. In the present study, acute and 28-day repeat-dose toxicity of Vernolac were evaluated in Wist...

title: Effects of probiotic supplementation on serum zonulin levels in patients with chronic kidney disease: a randomized clinical trial.
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with intestinal dysbiosis, systemic inflammation, and impaired intestinal barrier function. Serum zonulin has been proposed as an indirect marker of intestinal permeability, although its clinical relevance in CKD remains uncertain.

title: Bacillus subtilis PB43 prevents enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC)-induced diarrhea in mice by modulating the gut microbiota and metabolic profiles.
abstract: Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC) is a major pathogenic bacterium that can cause infectious diarrhea and poses a significant threat to intestinal health. Bacillus subtilis PB43, which was isolated from fecal samples of healthy pigs in regions with endemic diarrhea, has demonstrated notable probiotic properties. This study aims to investigate the preventive effects of PB43 and its influencing factors on diarrhea induced by ETEC. The findings revealed that PB43 alleviated ETEC-induced weight...

title: Genomic insights into the probiotic safety, butyrate production, and type-II L-Asparaginase of Bacillus altitudinis AHK-Y5.
abstract: Bacillus altitudinis is a resilient, spore-forming, Gram-positive bacterium. It thrives in soil, water, air, plant roots, and the human gut. It is a potential candidate for various industrial, biomedical, and biotechnological applications. This study analyzes an airborne B. altitudinis strain, AHK-Y5 for genome-based safety assessment (GBSA), and production and in silico analysis of L-asparaginase. The genome has 3.7 million base pairs and 3,822 genes. It lacks virulence and drug resistance gene...

title: Conformational and Rheological Changes of Hericium erinaceus Polysaccharides Driven by Molecular Weight Reduction and Their Impact on Prebiotic Effects.
abstract: Hericium erinaceus polysaccharide was degraded using microwave-assisted enzymatic hydrolysis to obtain four gradient molecular weight fractions (HePs). This study investigated the effects of molecular weight on their structural, rheological, and prebiotic properties. The reduction in molecular weight preserved the monosaccharide composition, functional groups, and residue types but significantly decreased their apparent viscosity and converted spatial conformations from compact and rigid triple-...
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Human Milk-Derived Synbiotics Attenuate DSS-Induced Colitis in Mice via Promoting Intestinal Colonization of Lachnospira.
abstract: 2'-Fucosyllactose (2'-FL) exhibits prebiotic properties, but its ability to enhance probiotic efficacy in ulcerative colitis (UC) is incompletely understood. Here, we show that 2'-FL effectively enhances the protective effect of Bifidobacterium bifidum B-67 against DSS-induced colitis in mice. Combination therapy outperformed individual treatments, suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokines and restoring mucosal integrity. Mechanistically, 2'-FL remodeled the gut microbiota, enriched butyrate-produc...
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Microwave-Induced Improvement in the Structural Compactness of Starch-Lauric Acid-Whey Protein Ternary Complexes: Enhanced Encapsulation of Butyl Butyrate and Prebiotic Potential of the Quaternary Complex.
abstract: Starch-based multicomponent complexes are promising carriers for functional molecules, but their limited stability and encapsulation efficiency constrain practical applications. Microwave (MW)-pretreated starch and whey protein (WP) were assembled with lauric acid to form a ternary complex (MTC), followed by butyl butyrate (BB) loading to produce MTC-B. Characterization and molecular dynamics simulations showed that MW altered amylopectin branching and partially unfolded WP, strengthening hydrog...
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Inositol for infertile women with polycystic ovary syndrome.
abstract: This is an update of a previously published review. Women with infertility may use adjunctive therapies to improve reproductive outcomes. Myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol are dietary supplements widely available and commonly used by women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS; renamed polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) in May 2026). The use of inositol for women with PCOS and infertility is based on proposed effects on insulin sensitivity and ovarian function. In clinical practice, ...
journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews

title: Dietary patterns, supplements, and physical activity in hidradenitis suppurativa: A scoping review.
abstract: The relationship between diet, physical activity, and hidradenitis suppurative remains underexplored.

title: Effects of a Probiotic Combination Containing Lacticaseibacillus paracasei BEPC22 and Lactiplantibacillus plantarum BELP53 on Body Fat Reduction: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study in Adults with Overweight.
abstract: Obesity is a major global health concern associated with increased risks of metabolic disorders, cardiovascular diseases, and reduced quality of life. Although lifestyle modification remains the cornerstone of obesity management, there is growing interest in safe and effective nutritional interventions that can support body fat reduction. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of HH202-LB (formerly BN-202M), a probiotic combination containing Lacticaseibacillus paracasei BEPC22 and Lactipl...

title: Probiotic-based sequential delivery system for gut-brain co-therapy against inflammatory bowel disease-associated anxiety/depression.
abstract: With the emergence of the gut-brain axis, inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is no longer simply regarded as a localized intestinal disease but as a systemic disorder intimately associated with psychiatric comorbidities, including anxiety and depression. However, conventional therapeutic strategies predominantly target localized colonic inflammation, which often yields suboptimal outcomes. This highlights a critical need for gut-brain co-therapy to achieve comprehensive IBD management. Based on ou...

title: Systems Biology Models in Microbiome Therapeutics.
abstract: Systems biology is an approach that integrates omics technologies such as genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and metagenomics with computational modelling tools for understanding complex biological systems. Systems biology approaches help to understand and capture dynamic interactions between microbial communities and the host, including metabolic cross-feeding, predicting emergent properties, and ecological relationships that influence host health and disease. This chapter rev...
journal: Advances in experimental medicine and biology

title: Virtual Screening of Microbiome Modulators: Mechanisms, Computational Approaches, and Therapeutic Applications.
abstract: The human gut microbiome regulates metabolism, immunity, and brain function through interactions between microbes and the host. Probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics, and postbiotics reshape these communities to influence systemic health outcomes. These interventions address gut inflammation, obesity, infections, neurological disorders, and cancer. Virtual screening identifies compounds that target microbial or host-microbe pathways with high efficiently. This review describes modulator mechanisms ...
journal: Advances in experimental medicine and biology

title: Probiotics, Prebiotics, Synbiotics and the Gut-Brain Axis in Precision Health.
abstract: The gastrointestinal system synthesizes a considerable proportion of the body's neurotransmitters and neuromodulators and is consequently increasingly acknowledged as the "second brain." Advances in high-throughput sequencing technology following the Human Genome Project have considerably expanded understanding of the gut microbiome, igniting increasing interest in microbiota-based medicinal approaches. Probiotics, defined as live microorganisms offering health benefits when provided in suitable...
journal: Advances in experimental medicine and biology

title: Formulation Matters: Nutrient Availability and Label Accuracy of Supplements for Age-Related Macular Degeneration.
abstract: AREDS2-based supplements can reduce progression to advanced AMD, but commercially available supplements can differ in characteristics. The aim of this study was to compare two AMD supplements with different coatings for their effects on serum lutein and zeaxanthin (L&Z) levels, and to analyze commercially available supplements for label accuracy and levels of AREDS2-relevant nutrients.

title: Adjunctive supplementation with vitamin E, zinc, L-arginine, L-citrulline, coenzyme Q10, and selenium enhances testicular recovery after Palomo varicocelectomy with indocyanine green in adolescents: a retrospective analysis.
abstract: Varicocele in adolescents is associated with impaired testicular development and reduced fertility potential. Indocyanine green (ICG)- assisted Palomo varicocelectomy improves surgical precision by enhancing lymphatic visualization, but the contribution of postoperative nutraceutical supplementation to testicular recovery remains uncertain. A retrospective comparative analysis was conducted on sixty adolescents undergoing Palomo varicocelectomy. Thirty patients treated in 2024 received postopera...
journal: La Pediatria medica e chirurgica : Medical and surgical pediatrics

title: Effects of a multistrain probiotic formulation on immune response and microbiome modulation following influenza vaccination in adults: a randomised, triple-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
abstract: Seasonal influenza remains a major global health burden, despite widespread vaccination. Vaccine responsiveness varies considerably between individuals and is increasingly recognised to be influenced by host factors, including the gut microbiome. Probiotics have been proposed as a strategy to modulate microbiome-immune interactions, although their effects on vaccine responses and the underlying microbial mechanisms remain incompletely understood.

title: Prebiotics and the gut-bone marrow axis: potential remodeling of the hematopoietic/leukemic stem cell niche via short-chain fatty acids and AhR signaling.
abstract: Gut microbiota metabolites, such as short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) and tryptophan-derived indole ligands of the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR), can enter the circulation and modulate the bone marrow microenvironment, influencing hematopoietic and immune homeostasis. Recent studies suggest that these metabolites may reach the bone marrow and affect the hematopoietic and leukemic stem cell (HSC/LSC) niche. Increasing evidence indicates that the gut microbiome influences bone marrow hematopoiesis...

title: [Dietary Rhythm Disruption and Probiotic Intervention in Metabolic-Associated Fatty Liver Disease: Role of the Bmal1-Gut Microbiota-Liver Axis].
abstract: This study explored how dietary rhythms influence metabolic-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) progression and the interactions among the circadian gene Bmal1, the gut microbiota, and MAFLD.

abstract: To explore the efficacy of composite Microecologics on colitis in rat with Crohn's disease (CD) induced by 2, 4, 6-trinitrobenzene sulfonic acid (TNBS) and their impact on the intestinal flora.

title: Anthocyanin-rich black chokeberry (aronia melanocarpa) supplementation modulates exercise-induced changes in iron metabolism in female swimmers.
abstract: Intense exercise may transiently alter iron metabolism through inflammatory and oxidative mechanisms. Anthocyanin-rich black chokeberry (Aronia melanocarpa) may influence these responses and short-term iron regulation. This study evaluated the effects of black chokeberry supplementation on iron metabolism, inflammation, antioxidant capacity, and hematological status in female competitive swimmers.
journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

title: Effect of Spent Coffee Grounds Supplementation in Finishing Holstein Steers on the Reduction of Urinary Struvite Crystal Formation.
abstract: This study investigated the effect of supplementing the diet of Holstein steers with spent coffee grounds and its effects on general health, urine pH, urine specific gravity, urinary epithelial cell count, and urine crystal appearance rate, with the aim of examining the preventive effects against bovine urolithiasis. title: Ferric ion-mediated sodium carboxymethyl cellulose/metal-phenolic dual-network nanogels for probiotic encapsulation and delivery.
abstract: To enhance the tolerance of probiotics to adverse gastrointestinal conditions and improve their intestinal adhesion, we successfully developed a sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC)-based dual-network probiotic encapsulation system via a ferric ion (Fe3+)-mediated self-assembly strategy, integrating tannic acid (TA)/Fe3+ metal-phenolic networks (MPNs) to achieve multifunctional synergy. title: Structural characterization and comparative prebiotic potential of Anacardium occidentale gums polysaccharides extracted via diverse media.
abstract: Cashew tree gum (CTG) is a complex polysaccharide exudate with great industrial potential. This study systematically characterized CTG polysaccharides (CTGPs) extracted from nine African samples using three extraction media: hot water, sodium hydroxide (NaOH), and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2). The physicochemical properties, structural features, and in vitro fermentation profiles of the CTGPs were further compared with those of commercial gum Arabic (GA). title: Daily iron supplementation for prevention or treatment of iron-deficiency anaemia in infants, children, and adolescents.
abstract: Globally, 604.8 million women and 269 million children are living with anaemia; reducing anaemia is a key goal of the 2030 Global Strategy for Women's, Children's, and Adolescents' Health.
journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews

title: Effects of different dietary linseed supplementation forms on growth performance, carcass characteristics, meat quality, and nutritional composition of qinchuan beef cattle.
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of dietary cold-pressed linseed cake supplementation on growth performance, carcass traits, meat quality, and nutritional composition in Qinchuan beef cattle. Eighteen healthy 18-month-old cattle (282 ± 10 kg) were randomly assigned to three dietary treatments (n = 6): a control diet (CON), a diet supplemented with 12% cold-pressed linseed cake (CLC), and a diet supplemented with 12% crushed linseed (CLS). The trial consisted of a 15-day adaptation period...

title: Effectiveness of a Nutritional Supplement With Anti-Inflammatory Compounds and Olive Oil in Malnourished Patients.
abstract: Disease-related malnutrition (DRM) with systemic inflammation is associated with poor clinical outcomes and muscle mass loss. This study in a real-world clinical practice examined whether an oral nutritional supplement (ONS) enriched with anti-inflammatory compounds-eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) and extra-virgin olive oil (EVOO)-was associated with improvements in nutritional status, muscle mass and functional performance in patients with inflammation-related DRM.
journal: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle

title: Effect of Spent Coffee Grounds Supplementation on Meat Quality in Finishing Holstein Steers.
abstract: This study evaluated the effects of feeding spent coffee grounds on blood antioxidant capacity and meat quality in finishing steers. Twenty Holstein steers were assigned to two groups. For 4 months prior to slaughter, the supplemented group received 600 g/day of spent coffee grounds added to a basal diet, whereas the control group received the basal diet only.
